title: Activation sculpting and calibration harness for model-specific outlier mitigation
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Build an extensible calibration harness and activation-sculpting pipeline to generate model-specific FP8/INT8 quantization profiles and layer-wise scale fixes for Llama, Mistral, and Qwen families. Focus is on identifying per-head/layer outliers, applying data-driven sculpting (percentile annealing + residual-aware scaling), and producing guarded profiles that meet accuracy SLAs while enabling aggressive int8/fp8 compression. Deliverables: calibration harness, profile generator, regression test suite, and automated validation dashboard integration.
acceptance_criteria: Profile generator can produce model-specific FP8 and INT8 profiles for at least Llama-2-13B, Mistral-7B-v0.1, and Qwen-7B with deterministic outputs given seed
End-to-end pipeline produces quantized models with <0.7% perplexity regression on standard LLM eval suite and <0.5% accuracy regression on our conversational benchmark compared to float32 baseline
Layer-wise scale reconciliation reduces catastrophic activations in top-3 offending layers by >80% (measured by tail L2 mass) without manual per-model tuning
Automated calibration runs surface a suggested guardrail (head clipping percentile + scale anneal) and export as runtime-compatible profile JSON
Calibration runs are integrated into CI and regression dashboard; any profile that increases error beyond thresholds blocks promotion
implementation_notes: Calibration harness will sample adversarial and production-like prompts: SFT dialogs, code, and instruction-following queries pulled from golden dataset buckets
Activation sculpting strategy: per-head percentile clipping followed by residual-aware layer scale adjustment; percentile annealing schedule across mini-batches to avoid brittle clipping
Profile exporter produces: per-layer scale, per-head clip percentiles, quantization zero-point heuristics, and recommended fallback variants
We will reuse existing kernel-selection hooks to pick int8/fp8 kernels and ensure mappings to runtime kernel names are stable
Performance budget: keep additional inference overhead <4% by preferring simple per-channel rescale and avoiding expensive runtime branching
Tooling: python harness + Torch/ONNX conversion path + small C++ validator that mimics runtime quant kernels for quick CI checks
testing_plan: Unit test activation sculpting logic with synthetic activations that include controlled outliers
Run full calibration on Llama-2-13B, Mistral-7B, Qwen-7B using 1k warm prompts and 10k validation prompts; compare token-level perplexity and prompt-level accuracy
A/B experiment in staging serving: serve small percentage (2%) of traffic with quantized profile and monitor token-error, latency, and cost per thousand tokens
Create regression dashboard with per-prompt delta histograms, aggregate MRR-style metric, and incident alerting when >0.5% of prompts exhibit >2x token-error
Include randomized stability tests: +/-5% scaling noise to ensure profiles are robust to small kernel numeric variations
rollout_plan: Phase 1: Local experiments and CI integration (this ticket) — create profiles and automated checks
Phase 2: Staging A/B with limited model variants and close monitoring (2% traffic) — 2 weeks
Phase 3: Gradual rollout to 25% and then 100% for models that pass regression gates; pair with fallback policies (runtime auto-fallback to fp16)
Phase 4: Package profiles into repo and document per-model recommendations in Console and release notes

metrics: Target: token-perplexity regression <0.7% vs float32 baseline
Target: conversational accuracy delta <0.5% on golden benchmark
Tail metric: reduce top-0.1% activation energy by >80% in offending layers
Performance: end-to-end inference latency increase <4% when activation sculpting runtime flags enabled
risks: Over-aggressive clipping could silently degrade specific prompt types (code generation, math) — mitigated by adversarial sets
Per-model manual tuning may creep if auto-suggested guardrails are insufficient — plan to capture tuning configs in metadata
Runtime mismatch: profile field name drift between harness and runtime may cause silent fallback — added compatibility layer and CI check
Quant kernels may exhibit nondeterminism on some hardware; include randomized noise tests in CI
